summary: This guide explains how to build menus around seasonal produce and regional recipes, written on September 10, 2023. It covers planning, working with local producers, staying flexible, educating staff and patrons, preserving food, using apps, and the sustainability benefits of eating seasonally. Chefs and other experts are quoted throughout.
one_line: A guide to crafting sustainable seasonal menus that adapt regional recipes to local produce, with expert advice on planning, flexibility, education and sustainability.
key_facts: The note is dated September 10, 2023, and fall begins on September 22, 2023.
Eating seasonally means enjoying produce at peak flavor and nutrition, such as strawberries in June and pumpkins in October.
Local horticulturist Emma Johnson says seasonal eating gives better-tasting ingredients and is environmentally sound and economically beneficial for local farmers.
Chef Marcus Williams recommends transitioning menus gradually by introducing a few seasonal dishes as new produce arrives.
Rachel Gomez, a chef with a farm-to-fork restaurant in the Midwest, says menus built on local availability push her creativity.
Producer connections can be built through farmers' markets, community-supported agriculture (CSA) groups, or trips to nearby farms.
A classic ratatouille can swap butternut squash in for zucchini in the fall.
Chef Aiden Clarke suggests a slow-roasted tomato dish instead of a raw tomato salad if the week's tomatoes are not ripe enough.
Thanksgiving on November 25, 2023, can feature roasted turkey with locally-sourced cranberry sauce and pumpkin pie made with pumpkins from a nearby farm.
Canning supplies and fermentation techniques preserve surplus produce, minimize waste, and extend seasonal tastes.
Apps such as 'Seasonal Food Guide' and 'Harvest: Select the Best Produce' help with seasonal ingredients, and blogger Sophia Rios says they can remind users when produce comes into season.
Dietitian Michaela Tran says a plant-forward seasonal menu conserves resources and reduces greenhouse gas emissions associated with meat production.
Servers should be able to explain the reasons behind seasonal ingredient shifts and the story of the local producer.
